$comment: Documented differences between the three Content Security Policies compared by scripts/check-csp-parity.mjs (site and app-web from their vercel.json; desktop from tauri.conf.json). Each entry says in which policies a source is expected, and why it is absent from the others. A source present in every policy needs no entry. Keep the reasons honest: mark what is not verified.

exceptions.reason: Tauri's own schemes (tauri:, asset:, ipc:) exist only inside the desktop WebView. The desktop policy has no script-src, style-src or worker-src, so default-src carries what the web hosts put there: 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval' and blob: for the bundled engine and its workers.
The desktop policy has no script-src: scripts fall back to default-src, which allows 'self' and 'unsafe-inline'.
The site runs no WebAssembly. The desktop covers WebAssembly with 'unsafe-eval' in default-src.
Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon, loaded by the public site only.
The desktop policy has no style-src: styles fall back to default-src, which allows 'self' and 'unsafe-inline'.
The desktop policy has no font-src: fonts fall back to default-src, which allows 'self'.

Alice Web embeds icon fonts as data URIs; the site serves its fonts from files. Not verified: the desktop bundles Alice Web but its default-src has no data:, so a data: font in the desktop build would be reported. Check with the crawl script before enforcing.
Tauri's asset protocol, desktop only.
QR codes and generated images are drawn from blobs in the apps; the site shows no generated image.
Learn pack illustrations come from the packs repository (raw.githubusercontent.com) and its jsDelivr mirror; Alice Web and its desktop build share them. The site loads no remote image.
Tauri IPC, and a local model server on a loopback port (the AI tab accepts a server URL such as http://localhost:11434/v1). A web page must not reach loopback hosts.

The desktop can call Venice directly through the alice-ai Venice transport; the web hosts go through the Worker (proxy.alicebtc.com) only. Not verified that the desktop build still uses the direct path.
The site posts its analytics beacon to Cloudflare and calls the Worker by its exact host; the apps allow https://*.alicebtc.com instead.

The Worker, the semantic model files, Esplora (mainnet for Explorer, Mutinynet for the Playground) and the Arkade operators (Explorer) are used by Alice Web and its desktop build. The public site needs none of them. Alice Web reaches them through its scheme-wide connect-src (see the https: entry), so its policy names no host.

Alice Web's enforced policy (docs/security/web-storage-hardening.md) allows any HTTP(S) or WebSocket destination because Custom AI endpoints and custom Explorer nodes are chosen by the user. It does not prevent exfiltration by code that already runs. The desktop keeps a host list, and does not list raw.githubusercontent.com (Learn markdown) or api.coinbase.com (price feed): whether the desktop build fetches them is not verified, to confirm with the crawl script on the desktop.

Learn packs (jsDelivr), the Private Cloud attestation (Intel) and the explorer providers (Esplora mirrors, Liquid, Ark, Spark) belong to Alice Web and its desktop build; Alice Web reaches them through its scheme-wide connect-src. The site has no explorer and no Learn.

The Satora swap provider on Mutinynet. No source in this repository calls it: the Playground is on-chain only, with no swap. The desktop policy still names it; left as found, a candidate for removal, not verified.
The semantic engine runs in workers built from blobs. The site has no worker. The desktop has no worker-src: workers fall back to default-src, which allows 'self' and blob:.
Learn embeds videos through the privacy-enhanced YouTube player, in Alice Web and its desktop build; the site embeds nothing.
A Tauri WebView cannot be framed by a web page, so the desktop policy leaves this navigation directive out. It has no default-src fallback.
The desktop bundle sets no base element and navigates only its own files; the directive has no default-src fallback.
Alice Web's enforced policy forbids any base element, a stricter value than the site's report-only 'self'. The desktop leaves the directive out (see the 'self' entry).
The desktop bundle submits no HTML form to a remote host; the directive has no default-src fallback.
The desktop policy has no object-src: plugins fall back to default-src. No plugin is loaded on any surface.
